paper.title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
paper.central_claim: A frozen-LLM planner-executor agent with an online-growing episodic case bank and a learned case-retrieval Q-policy (memory-based online RL, M-MDP) continually improves deep-research performance without fine-tuning the LLM: GAIA val 87.88% Pass@3 / test 79.40%, DeepResearcher 66.6 F1 / 80.4 PM, case memory adds 4.7-9.6 points on OOD sets.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref unavailable to worker in this runtime; model_type is the controller-configured slot (haiku agent type -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

rationale: LLM冻结，案例库+Q检索。K=4与OOD有限增益；GAIA记忆建于验证集且为Pass@3，无种子/CI、无写入门控，w/o CBR随迭代也涨，归因偏弱。

evidence.quote: In contrast, our method enables low-cost continual adaptation via memory-based online reinforcement learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Central claim: continual adaptation via memory, not LLM updates.

evidence.quote: However, most systems keep adding cases without selective curation, leading to the classic swamping problem where retrieval costs outweigh utility
evidence.support_explanation: Authors name the residual (uncurated growth, retrieval cost > utility) they position against.

evidence.quote: In the parametric setting, Write further online updates a Q-function to shape the retrieval distribution, while Read is driven by the learned Q-function, thereby realising adaptive case selection.
evidence.support_explanation: Write/Read operations of the parametric memory: Q-network is the retained, updated retrieval policy.

evidence.quote: the case memory is updated with new experiences only upon task completion.
evidence.support_explanation: Write trigger: end of task, not per step.

evidence.quote: only the state, action, and reward from the final step of each trajectory are written to memory, ensuring that the case bank remains both compact and informative.
evidence.support_explanation: Case unit = (task, final plan, success). No admission gate other than the reward label; failures are stored too.

evidence.quote: For the GAIA validation evaluation, we initialise memory from scratch and iteratively store both successful and failed trajectories in the case bank over three iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline GAIA-validation number is measured while the memory is built on the same 150 validation questions.

evidence.quote: For the GAIA test set, performance is based solely on the case bank accumulated during validation, yielding an accuracy of
evidence.support_explanation: Test set is separated from bank construction (private leaderboard).

evidence.quote: pairing the fast, non-deliberative GPT-4.1 planner with the o3 executor yields the highest average accuracy (70.9%)
evidence.support_explanation: Same GPT-4.1+o3 configuration gives 70.9% at pass@1 vs the 87.88% Pass@3 headline.

evidence.quote: The impact of fast and slow think mode on GAIA validation dataset (pass@1).
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms the 70.9% is pass@1 on validation.

evidence.quote: We first collect and store trajectories from the training datasets in the case bank.
evidence.support_explanation: OOD protocol: bank built on NQ/TQ/HotpotQA/2Wiki, evaluated on MusiQue/Bamboogle/PopQA.

evidence.quote: achieves substantial improvements on all OOD benchmarks, with absolute gains ranging from 4.7% to 9.6%.
evidence.support_explanation: Author-reported OOD gain range (per-benchmark values only in Fig.1d, not extractable from the text).

evidence.quote: – yielding the highest F1 (64.5) and PM (78.5) – but plateaus or slightly declines for larger
evidence.support_explanation: K=4 best, larger K plateaus/declines.
Columns K=0,1,2,4,8,16,32 (F1,PM): K=4 vs K=0 = +4.6 F1 / +6.3 PM on DeepResearcher (store-off vs store-on).
Row w/o CBR: avg 59.9/72.2 (equals Table 3 K=0).
Full Memento avg 66.6/80.4 (differs from Table 3 K=4 = 64.5/78.5; configuration difference not stated).

evidence.quote: Baseline Memento w/o CBR 78.65 80.93 82.62 83.53 84.47
evidence.support_explanation: Without case memory the metric still rises 78.65 -> 84.47 over five iterations (+5.8), unexplained.

evidence.quote: Memento w/ Non-Parametric CBR 79.84 81.87 83.09 84.03 84.85
evidence.support_explanation: kNN-retrieval CBR gain over w/o CBR per iteration: +1.19, +0.94, +0.47, +0.50, +0.38.

evidence.quote: Memento w/ Parametric CBR 80.46 82.84 84.10 84.85 85.44
evidence.support_explanation: Q-retrieval gain over w/o CBR: +1.81, +1.91, +1.48, +1.32, +0.97; over kNN only +0.6 to +1.0.

evidence.quote: In our simulated, open-ended, but ultimately finite environment, we observe rapid convergence with only marginal gains after a few iterations.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede saturation/marginal gains.

evidence.quote: For DeepResearcher, we also identify data contamination
evidence.support_explanation: Authors detect contamination of DeepResearcher benchmarks for the backbone LLMs.

evidence.quote: Without bootstrapping, the updating reduces to a supervised learning paradigm, which avoids non-stationary targets.
evidence.support_explanation: The practical parametric retriever is a single-step supervised success classifier, not multi-step soft-Q.

evidence.quote: and implement the Q-function as a two-layer MLP to assign the Q value.
evidence.support_explanation: Retained learned component = small MLP over frozen SimCSE embeddings (non-LLM weights).

evidence.quote: Memento (w/o CBR) keeps episodic memory disabled, allowing us to measure the extra gain delivered specifically by case-based reasoning.
evidence.support_explanation: The memory-off control used throughout (same planner/executor/tools).

evidence.quote: The results of prompt-based and training-based methods using Qwen
evidence.support_explanation: Training-based DeepResearcher baselines are Qwen2.5-7B systems; Memento uses GPT-4.1+o4-mini+tools, so Table 1 is not like-for-like.

evidence.quote: This highlights that the primary computational burden in complex scenarios stems from integrating and analysing multi-step tool outputs, rather than from generating long responses.
evidence.support_explanation: Only token cost of the whole GAIA agent is reported; no memory-specific or matched-budget cost.

evidence.quote: Ablation studies reveal that both parametric and non-parametric CBR are critical to the significant performance gains, and that a small, curated memory yields optimal results.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors' own summary contrasts with the implemented bank (no curation, K-cap only).

G.reason: Real but generic gap (static/handcrafted vs gradient-tuned agents); concrete residue (swamping, similarity!=utility) is named, yet nearest neighbours (ExpeL, AWM, Mem0, A-MEM, Agent-KB...) are only cited, not compared; the new retriever answers 'utility vs resemblance' but not 'swamping'.

M.reason: Mechanism reconstructable (write final-step case, rank by learned Q, inject top-K) but the M-MDP/soft-Q formalism collapses to a single-step BCE classifier and credit assumes the retrieved case caused the outcome; no distinguishing prediction vs plain kNN is stated.

X.reason: Write/read steps and K are explicit and code is announced, but no admission gate, versioning, dedup, retirement/staleness or rollback; text is inconsistent on what is stored (per step in §3 vs final step only in §5.3); bank stays unbounded.

E.measurement.reason: GAIA exact-match via leaderboard is solid, but DeepResearcher/HLE/SimpleQA rely on GPT-4o-mini F1/PM judging and the authors detect backbone contamination on DeepResearcher; Table 1 compares with 7B trained systems.

E.causality.reason: Memory-off (K=0/w/o CBR) ablation and NP-vs-P are reported, but no matched retry/budget control (Pass@3 and iterations), no abstraction-based or random-case control, and Table 4 shows large iteration-driven gains without memory; P-vs-NP difference <1 point from a single run.

E.holdout.reason: OOD protocol (bank from 4 datasets, test on 3) is a real separation, but the GAIA-val headline and Table 4 curve use a bank built on the evaluated stream, bank source for HLE/SimpleQA is unstated, and no overlap audit exists.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes and some negative results (K>4 plateau, saturation, Level-3 weakness, contamination) are reported, but every headline is a single run without seeds/CI, and differences of 0.4-1 point are interpreted.

E.cost.reason: Only whole-agent GAIA token costs are given; no memory-specific cost, no matched-budget/Pass@k parity, planner+executor LLMs far stronger than the trained 7B baselines.
